# Recap: our call on 6 October 2026

## Today
Purchase orders arrive by email as PDFs, and your order coordinator types each one into the shared order sheet; at the end of the day your bookkeeper types it again into QuickBooks Online to invoice it. The same product code is written several ways in that sheet, so every Monday the codes are corrected by hand. When a code is wrong, the wrong tile ships and you hear about it from the job site; last month that meant three reshipped pallets, about $1,800.

## What needs to change
Every order is confirmed the same day it arrives, and no pallet is reshipped because of a wrong code. Your biggest customer needs that in place by 1 March, when its spring orders start.

## Next step
I recommend a Build Plan covering two systems: your order sheet and QuickBooks Online. The product codes need cleaning up and the 1 March date leaves no room for a second false start, so the approach is worth mapping before anything is built. If you say yes, I'll send a one-page offer for the Build Plan with its fee and dates, and we'll start from a short list of samples you send.

## What I need from you
- Is there a budget range set aside for this, or are we building the case for one?
- In a normal week, is it closer to 60 orders or 90?
- Two or three recent purchase orders as they arrived, so I can see how the product codes come in.

## Promised by me
- A short list of what I need to see from QuickBooks.

Robin
